conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
THE CHLORIDE SHIFT (AT TISSUE LEVEL)
                    
   INTERSTITIAL TISSUE                          RED BLOOD CELL (RBC)
   CO2 ───────────────────────────────────────► CO2 + H2O
                                                  │
                                        [Carbonic Anhydrase]
                                                  │
                                                H2CO3
                                                  │
                                                H+ + HCO3-
                                                │     │
                   [Hb Buffering: H+ + Hb ──► HHb]    └──────► Diffuses OUT into Plasma
                                                                │
   Plasma Cl- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──► Diffuses INTO RBC
                                                                     (via Anion Exchanger 1 / AE1)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Carbon dioxide generated by tissue respiration is transported in blood in three forms:
1. **Dissolved in Plasma ($7\%$)**
2. **Carbamino-Hemoglobin ($20\text{--}25\%$)**: Bound to N-terminal amino groups of globin chains ($\text{Hb-NH-COOH}$).
3. **Bicarbonate Ions ($\text{HCO}_3^-, 70\%$)**: Hydrated inside RBCs by Carbonic Anhydrase.

- **Physiological Delivery**: $100\text{ mL}$ of deoxygenated blood delivers $\approx 4\text{ mL of }\text{CO}_2$ to alveoli.

### 7.1 The Hamburger Phenomenon (Chloride Shift)
- In tissue capillaries, Carbonic Anhydrase ($\text{Zn}^{2+}$ enzyme) hydrates $\text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{H}^+ + \text{HCO}_3^-$.
- $\text{HCO}_3^-$ diffuses OUT of the RBC into plasma down its gradient via the **Anion Exchanger 1 (AE1 / Band 3)** protein.
- To maintain electroneutrality, **Chloride ions ($\text{Cl}^-$) diffuse from plasma INTO the RBC** (**Chloride Shift**).
- **Reversal at Alveolar Capillaries**: In pulmonary capillaries, low $p\text{CO}_2$ causes $\text{Cl}^-$ to exit RBCs, $\text{HCO}_3^-$ to enter, and Carbonic Anhydrase regenerates $\text{CO}_2$ to diffuse into alveoli.
- **The Haldane Effect**: Oxygenation of hemoglobin in alveoli decreases its affinity for $\text{CO}_2$, displacing carbamino-$\text{CO}_2$ and protons to facilitate rapid $\text{CO}_2$ unloading.
